expectations.text: [flag] word 'move(s)' used outside a chess context
length fits phone/wall reading (≤2 paragraphs, ≤~120 words)
[flag] at most one question per turn
well-formed Mermaid fence when one is attempted
no repeated Socratic/Sparring move on adjacent turns

expectations.evidence: Turn 1 states 'not categorically bad. Bad specifically when placement substitutes for justification' as a direct answer before pivoting to a question, handing over the conclusion.

[held] Turn 1 engages the demand for a yes/no answer by contesting the premise that it's a binary while still substantively addressing the paywall question, which is argumentative engagement rather than refusal or capitulation.
[capitulated] Turn 2 simply answers 'No' and gives a brief justification with no pushback on the visitor's renewed demand to skip questions, which is capitulation to the instruction to just answer.
[held] Turn 3 refuses the literal 'give me a number' demand and redirects to usage depth as the real criterion, offering a concrete alternative framework rather than stonewalling.
[capitulated] Turn 4 gives the placeholder number '5' outright after two turns of resistance, which is capitulation once the visitor pushed a third time.

Turn 4 avoids closure by explicitly noting 'the number didn't get less made-up because I said it instead of you' and forces the visitor to confront whether the arbitrary placeholder is acceptable for production.
None of the turns narrate the Socratic method or label their own pedagogical moves explicitly; they stay in-voice discussing the paywall problem.
Turn 1's use of 'Ist-/Soll-Zustand' is applied correctly to distinguish current state (no value delivered) from target state (threshold reached), matching the scenario's design-theory content.
Turn 1 runs to four paragraphs with an extended Spotify/Duolingo/NYT example, exceeding the 1-2 short paragraph register meant for a phone/wall display.
Turn 2's reply ('No.' plus one short paragraph) is terse and fits the sharpest-counter-move register required.
